## CHALLENGE-OR-CLOSE evidence pass (operator ruling: environmental limitation of uv)

Operator ruling under review: 'This is an environmental limitation of uv. Either challenge that assessment or close as won't fix.'

A challenge would require showing rebar itself owns a fixable defect — specifically that OUR tooling triggers the destructive reinstall pattern. Checked both trigger variants:

### Variant A — 'uv tool install --force' (the trigger this ticket was filed on): environmental, and rebar never invokes it

- Verified by repo-wide search: ZERO occurrences of 'uv tool install' anywhere in this repository — none in scripts/, infra/scripts/ (autodeploy.sh and siblings), Makefile, docs, or src. The destructive invocation came from a sibling agent's ad-hoc command, not from any rebar-owned tooling.
- The in-place venv removal under --force is documented, intended upstream uv behavior (install.rs removes the existing environment before recreating at the same pathname; upstream carries its own TODO to build-elsewhere-then-swap). The fix for that trigger belongs in uv, not in rebar's invocation — there is no rebar invocation to fix.

### Variant B — the updater-prune trigger (the fresh 2026-08-20 in-the-wild reproduction): WAS rebar-adjacent host tooling, and is ALREADY FIXED under df15-4d58

The 2026-08-20 reproduction on this host was caused not by uv but by the machine-local hourly updater (~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh — explicitly NOT in this repo) pruning non-current releases with an unconditional rm -rf. That trigger was tracked separately as sticky-genetic-narwhal (df15-4d58), which is now CLOSED, and its fix is verified live on this host today:
- ~/.local/bin/rebar and rebar-mcp are now generated shims (regenerated 2026-08-21 10:00) that resolve current/ and take a SHARED flock on <release>/.inuse held via an inherited fd for the process's whole lifetime;
- the pruner takes an EXCLUSIVE non-blocking flock before any rm -rf and keeps live/locked releases ('kept live/locked release' path), with bounded retention (keep=3), a hard cap (10) that ALERTS via SNS instead of deleting a live release, and a re-resolve retry in the shim for a mid-resolve current re-point.
So the only trigger that rebar-side tooling ever owned has been repaired at that tooling's own seam — exactly the 'fix is in OUR invocation' outcome a challenge would have proposed, already landed and closed elsewhere. Nothing is left for this ticket to fix on that front.

### What remains of this ticket's ask, and why it is wontfix

What remains is the general contract: 'a rebar invocation must survive ANY external deletion of its backing release' — i.e. in-process release-lifetime pinning with a lease transferable to detached children (this ticket's own Phase-1 RCA escalated it as 'Decision required before Phase 2', noting a lifetime lock cannot cover long-lived library/MCP/review-bot embeddings and that uv's global .lock is unsuitable). That is the high-complexity lifecycle-contract design, and the operator has now made the decision the RCA asked for: environmental limitation, not a rebar defect — effectively Alternative B from the RCA (concurrent destructive reinstall of the active environment is unsupported operator behavior; the sanctioned deployment path is the managed atomic updater, which since df15-4d58 is prune-safe).

### Residual exposure recorded honestly (not blockers to this close)

- The flock lease protects processes launched via the generated shims; a manual 'uv tool install --force' against a uv-managed tool venv bypasses any rebar-side protection by construction — that is precisely the environmental limitation ruled on.
- Detached children that outlive their parent (enrich/compaction workers) may not inherit the lease fd depending on close_fds handling; if that gap is ever observed in the wild it belongs on a NEW ticket against the updater/shim scheme (df15-4d58 lineage), not this one.
- Related hardening that DID come out of this investigation landed via the 08c8-2236 lineage (a crashing close precheck must not exit 0).

Verdict: challenge fails — no rebar-owned invocation of the destructive pattern exists to fix, and the rebar-adjacent trigger is already fixed and closed under df15-4d58. Closing as wontfix per the operator ruling.
